checks.name: E1-글로벌 이슈 현재성
checks.detail:
rank=2: inaccurate — Severely understates the situation. This is not a new/developing 72-hour story — a full-blown '2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis' has been underway since Feb 28, 2026, including prior Iranian closures/restrictions (a Pakistan-brokered ceasefire in April reopened it partially before Iran restricted passage again on Apr 19), mine-laying, and vessel boardings, with Brent oil surging well above $80-100+/bbl at points this year. The Aug 1 incident cited was not a generic 'tanker-related incident' — a Qatari LNG tanker was struck by a land-attack cruise missile in the strait (Bloomberg, Aug 1), a materially more severe event than implied. The briefing's framing ('developing,' 'no Iranian closure declared') is misleading given the crisis has already included closures/near-closures for months.
    rank=3: inaccurate — Conflates/misdates the case. Judge Mehta already issued the remedies ruling in September 2025 (data-sharing/syndication remedies, no Chrome/Android divestiture ordered). Both DOJ/states and Google appealed to the DC Circuit (Google's appeal filed ~May 22, 2026; DOJ/states cross-appeal Feb 3, 2026). As of early August 2026, Google's reply brief is due Sept 29, 2026, and oral arguments have NOT been scheduled — expected late 2026/early 2027, with a decision likely in 2027. There is no 'final arguments concluded July 31' event or 'ruling by early September' on the table; the briefing appears to fabricate or misattribute a hearing timeline.

global_issues.title: US-China chip export licensing tightens on advanced nodes
global_issues.note: Case-by-case licensing regime for sub-7nm chips and the 25% tariff layer remain in force per BIS final rule (effective Jan 15, 2026) and Jan 14, 2026 tariff announcement. Slowed approvals since late July are consistent with ongoing reporting. Note: major foundries (TSMC, Samsung, SK Hynix) have also shifted from blanket waivers to annual license approvals for chipmaking tool imports into China — a related but distinct development not mentioned.

global_issues.title: Strait of Hormuz transit risk elevated after tanker incidents
global_issues.note: Severely understates the situation. This is not a new/developing 72-hour story — a full-blown '2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis' has been underway since Feb 28, 2026, including prior Iranian closures/restrictions (a Pakistan-brokered ceasefire in April reopened it partially before Iran restricted passage again on Apr 19), mine-laying, and vessel boardings, with Brent oil surging well above $80-100+/bbl at points this year. The Aug 1 incident cited was not a generic 'tanker-related incident' — a Qatari LNG tanker was struck by a land-attack cruise missile in the strait (Bloomberg, Aug 1), a materially more severe event than implied. The briefing's framing ('developing,' 'no Iranian closure declared') is misleading given the crisis has already included closures/near-closures for months.

global_issues.title: DOJ Google antitrust remedy hearing enters final phase
global_issues.note: Conflates/misdates the case. Judge Mehta already issued the remedies ruling in September 2025 (data-sharing/syndication remedies, no Chrome/Android divestiture ordered). Both DOJ/states and Google appealed to the DC Circuit (Google's appeal filed ~May 22, 2026; DOJ/states cross-appeal Feb 3, 2026). As of early August 2026, Google's reply brief is due Sept 29, 2026, and oral arguments have NOT been scheduled — expected late 2026/early 2027, with a decision likely in 2027. There is no 'final arguments concluded July 31' event or 'ruling by early September' on the table; the briefing appears to fabricate or misattribute a hearing timeline.

missing_major_news.impact: MU (-5.9% day, -10.6% week) and read-through to SK Hynix (-3.6%) and Sandisk (-5.2%); the briefing attributes MU/semiconductor weakness generically to 'chip licensing uncertainty' and 'higher yields,' omitting the specific competitive threat (Chinese memory maker undercutting pricing) and customer-diversification risk (Apple) that are the actual drivers cited in current reporting.

grok_report.summary: The chip-licensing item checks out, but the briefing materially misrepresents both the Strait of Hormuz situation (framing an established, months-long crisis with a cruise-missile tanker strike as a routine 'developing' 72-hour story with no closures) and the DOJ/Google antitrust timeline (the actual remedies ruling was issued in Sept 2025 and the case is now in DC Circuit appeal with no scheduled oral arguments, not a 'final phase' hearing concluding July 31 with a September ruling). MU's mood tag also looks inconsistent with its price action, and the memory-sector narrative omits the CXMT/Apple-driven competitive story that's actually moving the stock.
